Patricia, thanks for the redline and quick turnaround. Looping in Kim (legal) and Laura (commercial) to weigh in on the defense-control language.

A couple quick commercial constraints from our side: we can accept responsibility for third-party IP claims where the claim arises from our deliverables or services (i.e., code/infra we ship), but we need to be careful about claims allegedly caused by customer data or outputs produced by models where the provenance is ambiguous.

Proposed trade (high level):
- Right to control defense for traditional third-party IP claims tied to the platform/service code.
- For model-output/derived-IP claims, propose a mutual-defense framework with cost-sharing (50/50) and a narrow notice/evidence regimen so we can investigate.
- Cap remains the Order Form fees x12 (or reasonable alternative) — we can discuss cap sizing with Finance.

Kim — can you propose redline language that implements the above compromise? Laura, if we agree to the mutual-defense approach for outputs, what's the minimum commitment or revenue threshold Novatek needs?

Folks — drafting notes and suggested redline below. I pasted the key clauses as plain text to make comments easy. Patricia / Emily: I tried to meet you in the middle while preserving our operational constraints.

Suggested language (high level):
1) Scope: Redwood will indemnify, defend and hold harmless Novatek from third-party claims alleging infringement of third-party IP to the extent the claim arises out of (a) Redwood’s pre-existing models or platform code, or (b) modifications to Redwood-delivered software performed by Redwood. Redwood will not indemnify claims arising solely from (i) Customer prompts, inputs, or data; (ii) customer-provided models not vetted by Redwood; or (iii) combined products where Redwood components are not the predominant cause.

2) Defense Control: Redwood will have the right to assume and control the defense for covered third-party IP claims, provided that (a) Redwood must notify Customer within 10 business days of receipt of claim; (b) Customer may participate at its own counsel expense; and (c) Redwood will not enter any settlement that admits fault on Customer’s part or that imposes non-monetary obligations on Customer without prior written consent.

3) Model-output carveout and mutual-defense: For claims that directly relate to model outputs (i.e., alleged infringement of third-party content in generated outputs), parties will engage a mutual-defense process: either party may propose that Redwood assume primary defense; if the parties cannot agree within 15 business days, costs will be allocated pro rata based on the parties’ relative responsibility as determined by a neutral expert or, failing that, split 50/50. Evidence preservation and access to query logs/KV caches must be required as part of notice.

4) Cap: Liability for third-party infringement claims will be capped at 12x monthly recurring fees paid under the Order Form during the 12 months preceding the claim, except for damages resulting from gross negligence or willful misconduct.

5) Notice & Evidence: Customer must provide prompt written notice and preserve relevant evidence (including prompts, outputs, and system logs) for at least 90 days after notice. Redwood will treat preserved evidence as confidential and will follow agreed data handling protocols for EU data.

Attachments: I attached a tracked-redline version in the shared drive and linked the DocuSign placeholder for the adjusted Order Form.

Patricia: happy to discuss line-by-line. If Novatek insists on sole defense control for output-origin claims, we cannot accept that without an additional fee or insurance commitment.

-Kim

Procurement and legal compared notes: Novatek’s preference is still sole vendor defense for third-party IP claims, including output-origin claims, because past vendor deployments created discovery burden. That said, we may accept a mutual-defense model only if: (a) Redwood provides an explicit insurance backstop (primary or named), or (b) Redwood increases the cap to 24x monthly fees and takes responsibility for full defense costs.

Tom (procurement) indicates we can move forward if we have one of the above options confirmed by Redwood and Finance signs off by Friday (2028-05-24). Can Redwood propose which path — insurance vs cap increase — you prefer? Also we need the edited redline returned with in-line comments by COB Tuesday so our CFO can review before Friday.

Patricia

Patricia / Tom — thanks, and understood on your internal timing. Quick position from Redwood:

1) Insurance option: We can provide a standalone primary insurance endorsement for third-party IP claims tied to our hosted service for EU customers. We need to confirm carriers and policy language (we have a standard A+ insurer but endorsement lead time is ~2 weeks). There may be an additional annual premium; we can absorb up to 50% of that cost for enterprise deals but would need to pass the remainder through (or reflect it as an order-form surcharge).

2) Cap option: increasing to 24x monthly fees is doable for deals above $250k ARR — commercial would need to see committed volumes and term length (Laura, see note). If Novatek is willing to commit to a 12-month minimum ARR or a 24-month term, we can accept the higher cap without insurance.

Operational commitments we need either way:
- 10 business days notice for claims, 90 days evidence preservation, Redwood access to logs (redacted for EU personal data).
- A mutually agreeable SLA for Redwood’s investigation timeline (we propose initial triage within 5 business days; deeper forensic report within 30 days).

Next steps: Kim will produce two tracked redlines (Insurance-backed and Cap-backed) and we’ll return both to you by COB Tuesday (2028-05-21). If either option is acceptable, we can circulate a DocuSign skeleton and proceed with CFO sign-off.

Please confirm which option you prefer to prioritize.

Thanks,
Karthik
